extraction.Name: Mrs. Aneline Brown Larvie
extraction.Refused/Protested: I got the patent fee thru the mail and kept it and made no protest because I did not what to do in the matter
extraction.Recorded patent: I do not know who record the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: the land was mortgaged and just before the same was due, I sold the land to pay off the mortgage and taxes
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: All of the land covered by patent was sold because I was not able to keep the taxes paid up
extraction.Occupation/Income: Partly supported by taking washing and scrubbing for people, and partly by my husbond's labor
extraction.NOTES: Received $3500.00 for the land but considers it not enough; did not owe the purchaser but was in debt elsewhere because people knew she had a patent in fee; mental conditions good but subject to kidney troubles; very poor financially; has one child wholly dependent upon husband and herself; blames the U.S. Government for the issuance of the patent which caused her to sell her Indian homestead before the trust period expired; patent received through the mail around March 26, 1920, no receipt given; document is an application for cancellation of Forced Patent In Fee | TASK 3 BULK TRIBE INFERENCE 2026-04-29: Tribe field set to 'Pine Ridge' based on directory provenance (record is filed in pine_ridge_*/extractions/, which corresponds to the NARA RG 75 Pine Ridge Vol 1, Vol 2, and Vol 3 bound volumes of Circular 2464 responses). 67 such records were originally 'not stated'; 6 received BLM-confirmed substantive patches in the same transaction; the remaining 61 (this record's batch) are inferred from directory and geographic/naming evidence. Inference is rebuttable — any record can be re-evaluated via BLM cross-reference if its Pine Ridge affiliation is questioned.
